title: Why I Keep Writing While Building

excerpt: Short notes help me ship more consistently than a perfect doc ever could.
tags: Writing, Workflow, Shipping

---

I do not think writing is separate from building.

The fastest way to understand a feature is often to explain it in plain language. Once the explanation feels easy, the implementation usually becomes clearer too.

## What the notes give me

- A way to spot missing decisions.
- A record of tradeoffs I can revisit later.
- A small public trail of what I am learning.

That matters even on small projects. A short post can be enough to capture the shape of an idea before the details fade.

## Why it stays short

Long posts are useful when the topic needs depth. Most of the time, though, I only need enough writing to keep momentum.

The goal is not to publish perfectly polished essays. The goal is to keep shipping with some context attached.

## A simple loop

1. Build the thing.
2. Write down what changed.
3. Use the note to make the next version cleaner.

That loop keeps the work visible and makes it easier to return to later.
